dedupe_keys.name: rims ii regional input output multipliers bea

description: RIMS II, the Regional Input-Output Modeling System, is a regional economic model of the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis that produces multipliers measuring the effect of local demand shocks on total gross output, value added, earnings and employment. Investors, planners and officials use them to estimate the total impact of a project on a region, capturing further rounds of spending: building a road raises asphalt and concrete production, which raises mining, and new workers spend locally. It is produced by BEA; new multipliers released on 5 May 2026 are based on 2024 regional data and the 2017 national benchmark input-output accounts. Coverage is the United States: a regional order covers all industries for a region of one or more contiguous counties, and an industry order covers the 50 states and the District of Columbia. Multipliers are sold online at 520 dollars per region and 160 dollars per industry, with a user guide and sample tables available. Caveats: multipliers are static and assume no supply constraints, and they cost money unlike most BEA data. For simulation they convert direct losses from infrastructure outages or disasters into total regional economic impacts. It is related to the BEA industry input-output accounts record in this catalogue, the national tables underneath.
